subject: Provisional SLA grace request — ClearPulse p95 tail anomaly (model omega-2.4)
messages:
From: Julie Hart <julie.hart@clearpulse.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+oncall@clearpulse.com
Date: 2029-11-02T14:23:00Z
Subject: Re: production anomalies — p95 spike after last deploy

Sergio —

We started seeing a sharp p95 latency increase (~350ms -> ~820ms) across a subset of inference calls after you rolled model omega-2.4 into our dedicated pool at 14:00 UTC. The traffic pattern is normal (no traffic surge), but the tail is concentrated on longer-sequence requests (>1k tokens).

Attached is a short query log excerpt and the canary metrics. This is impacting a real-time feature (document summarization) and we're now hitting our customers' latency SLA. Please advise: can you either roll back to the previous model (omega-2.3) or provide a mitigation plan and ETA? If we breach the SLA we may have to pursue credits, so we need an immediate path.

Thanks,
Julie Hart
Head of Integrations — ClearPulse
julie.hart@clearpulse.com

Attachments: slo-evidence-2029-11-02.pdf, query-snippet-omega2.4.log

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-11-02T15:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: production anomalies — p95 spike after last deploy

Kimberly / team — forwarding ClearPulse. I confirmed the spike on our side: p95 elevated from ~360ms to ~790ms for sequences >1k tokens on omega-2.4. Canary shows degradation only on their tenant's dedicated pool (no global regression).

Quick triage notes:
- Root suspicion: subtle attention kernel change in omega-2.4 interacting with long sequence dispatch path (KV cache miss amplification).
- Short term mitigations available: immediate traffic pin to omega-2.3 for ClearPulse, enable aggressive prefix caching on their routes, or enable the variant-fallback policy to auto-route to v2.3 when latency >600ms.
- Risk/cost: pinning will increase per-token cost for a short window; fallback is lower touch.

Ask: I want to request a provisional SLA grace (72h) while we either stabilize omega-2.4 or roll them back. Kimberly — can you authorize provisional grace and the mitigation (pin or fallback)? If approved, we'll notify ClearPulse and schedule the rollback window.

Quoted message:

> > We started seeing a sharp p95 latency increase (~350ms -> ~820ms) ...

Sergio

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Hart <julie.hart@clearpulse.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-11-02T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: production anomalies — p95 spike after last deploy

Julie — thanks for the alert and the artifacts. We're on this. Short plan we can execute immediately:

1) Enable variant fallback on your routing (route-level fallback to omega-2.3) — instant and non-disruptive.
2) If you prefer a hard rollback/pin, we can schedule a controlled pin to omega-2.3 (ETA 30 mins) and monitor for restoration.
3) We'll also turn on an aggressive prefix cache for your heavy sequences which should cut repeated KV misses.

Which approach do you prefer? If you approve fallback, we'll flip the policy immediately and monitor p95 for 30m, then report back. If you want the pin, reply with confirmation and we'll execute the pin and hold for a 1-hour observation window.

Subject: Re: production anomalies — p95 spike after last deploy — provisional grace approved

Approving provisional SLA grace for ClearPulse for a 72-hour window starting now. Authorization notes and conditions: 

- Approval scope: provisional SLA grace (latency p95 breaches only) for ClearPulse dedicated pool while we remediate or roll back. This is a one-off, conditioned approval tied to deal CP-2027-042.
- Required actions before grace activation: enable variant-fallback to omega-2.3 (Ben to execute) OR confirm scheduled pin. Sergio to confirm which mitigation was executed and post confirmation to RWD-1897.
- Monitoring and exit criteria: p95 back within 15% of baseline OR sustained improvement over 2 consecutive 30-min windows -> review and close grace early. If no improvement within 48 hours, escalate to exec review for potential credits.
- Documentation: full postmortem (root cause, fix, test plan) due within 7 business days. Attach evidence to ticket RWD-1897 and link to the HubSpot deal (CP-2027-042).

Ben — proceed with the fallback now and confirm. Sergio — once fallback is active, notify Julie and mark the grace window. Laura / Marcus — please prepare the rollback runbook and timeline in RWD-1897.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations — Redwood Inference
